# Twelve dinosaur dossiers without an ancestor ladder

## story / steps / annotation

<!-- evo:text /records/story/steps/0/annotation -->
The 233–228 Ma atlas interval is a display context for early dinosaur fossils, not an age inferred by either morphology matrix.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## story / steps / annotation

<!-- evo:text /records/story/steps/1/annotation -->
Formation correlation bounds the age; the dietary transition is a mapped hypothesis across sampled taxa, not a linear sequence observed in one lineage.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## story / steps / annotation

<!-- evo:text /records/story/steps/2/annotation -->
The broad display interval follows formation-level correlation and must not be read as a direct specimen date or a global ornithischian FAD.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## story / steps / annotation

<!-- evo:text /records/story/steps/3/annotation -->
The fossils constrain anatomy; centre of mass and stance are sensitivity-tested reconstructions and cannot be generalized to every sauropodomorph.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## story / steps / annotation

<!-- evo:text /records/story/steps/4/annotation -->
The specimen is incomplete and the earliest-Jurassic interval is formation-bounded; it is not a universal threshold or ancestor for sauropod gigantism.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## story / steps / annotation

<!-- evo:text /records/story/steps/5/annotation -->
Missing armour and preparation history prevent a complete in-place map; placement is one analysis rather than an uncontested thyreophoran topology.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## story / steps / annotation

<!-- evo:text /records/story/steps/6/annotation -->
The atlas interval is formation-level; topology and character polarity depend on outgroups, coding and the sampled matrix.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## story / steps / annotation

<!-- evo:text /records/story/steps/7/annotation -->
The evidence concerns one specimen and one depositional history; skin presence does not establish original colour, physiology or preservation frequency.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## story / steps / annotation

<!-- evo:text /records/story/steps/8/annotation -->
Non-avian integument stays here; Avialae, flight models and living-bird COL26.8 names remain owned by crocodylomorphs-birds.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## story / steps / annotation

<!-- evo:text /records/story/steps/9/annotation -->
The original paper explicitly retains alternative explanations and limits testing of parental-system hypotheses in the fossil record.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## story / steps / annotation

<!-- evo:text /records/story/steps/10/annotation -->
The 83–66 Ma atlas window spans sampled tyrannosaurids, not one population; the fitted curve is not a universal dinosaur growth schedule.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## story / steps / annotation

<!-- evo:text /records/story/steps/11/annotation -->
The models test capability rather than observe a feeding event; MOR 799 and the coprolite do not identify every individual or every feeding context.
<!-- /evo:text -->
